Q: How to update uniqueidentifier (GUID) from nvarchar in SQL Server (GUID with no dashes) A:

SQL Server can't convert it because it expects the standard GUID format with dashes.
If you need no-dash format, then store as VARCHAR. Must alter the table for that.
If the column should remain uniqueidentifier, just don't remove the dashes:

UPDATE a
SET GUID = b.guid
FROM table1 a 
JOIN table2 b ON a.ID = b.ID;

SQL Server will automatically handle the conversion since both columns are uniqueidentifier types.

Q: What is the best/recommended way to start and stop FlowReceiver in J2EE/JEE application? A:

For me, I would go for a more modern approach by using the Spring Cloud Stream. You don't need to rely on the CountDownLatch and there's also no endless loop to maintain (this is done at the library side internally).

The Solace tutorial site shows a sample using Spring Cloud Stream.

In this sample, the receiver stays always connected to the queue/topic.

Now if you just need to suspend the consumption in a nice way, I see two options:

  1. Use the Spring-Cloud Stream binding visualization control

    In this article from the Spring documentation you see different ways to manage this.

With Actuator it is quite simple:

1.1 Add the maven dependencies:

<dependency>
     <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
     <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
</dependency>

1.2 Enable the bindings actuator

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: bindings

1.3 Send REST request with curl to manager binders:

curl -d '{"state":"STOPPED"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST http://<host>:<port>/actuator/bindings/myBindingName
curl -d '{"state":"STARTED"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST http://<host>:<port>/actuator/bindings/myBindingName
curl -d '{"state":"PAUSED"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST http://<host>:<port>/actuator/bindings/myBindingName
curl -d '{"state":"RESUMED"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST http://<host>:<port>/actuator/bindings/myBindingName

  1. Use the Solace Egress settings.

    If you use queue or topic endpoint, you can suspend the message forwarding directly from the broker using the SEMPv2 API.

Example with the local instance:

curl -L -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/SEMP/v2/config/msgVpns/default/queues/THE-QUEUE \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Accept: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46YWRtaW4=' \
-d '{"egressEnabled": false}'

If you rely exclusively on topics (direct messaging), then the first solution could be the best option.

Q: From a root node, reaching all the next vertices with a specific label A:

You can

  • use all_simple_paths (or all_shortest_paths) + degree like below
f <- function(g, s) {
    unique(
        unlist(
            lapply(
                all_simple_paths(g, s, V(g)[V(g)$color == "red"]),
                function(x) {
                    r <- x$color == "red"
                    if (any(r)) {
                        x[which.max(r)]
                    }
                }
            )
        )
    )
}

such that

> f(g, 1)
[1] 8 9 5 3

> f(g, 6)
[1]  3 13

> f(g, 11)
[1] 5

> f(g, 7)
[1] 3
  • use ego like below
f <- function(g, s) {
    col <- V(g)$color
    v <- l <- s
    res <- c()
    repeat {
        if (is.null(v)) break
        vv <- unlist(ego(g, 1, v, mindist = 1))
        vv <- vv[!vv %in% l]
        idx <- col[vv] == "red"
        if (any(idx)) {
            res <- append(res, vv[idx])
        }
        v <- vv[!idx]
        l <- c(l, v)
    }
    res
}

such that

> f(g, 1)
[1] 3 5 8 9

> f(g, 6)
[1]  3 13

> f(g, 11)
[1] 5

> f(g, 7)
[1] 3
